newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to sell minimum 100 mln Ecu bonds per month.
newsitem.headline: France to sell minimum 100 mln Ecu bonds per month.

text.p: France will continue its regular Ecu OAT and BTAN auctions on the second Thursday of each month in the first half of 1997 but will auction Ecu bonds at the same time as French franc bonds in the second half of the year, the Treasury said in a statement.
It said the minimum amount of Ecu bonds to be sold per month in the first half would be 100 million Ecu.

The Treasury also said in the second half of the year it would try to match the characteristics - the coupon and maturity date - of new Ecu bond issues with franc bonds so that from January 1, 1999 they can be converted into a single Euro issue.
It also said France "may create, depending on market circumstances new (Ecu) issues to cover the whole of the yield curve better."

The Treasury said in the statement in addition to issuing 10-year franc bonds on the first Thursday of each month it may also issue, depending on market conditions, "other fixed-rate bonds or variable rates bonds in existence or to be created".
The statement said the Treasury was studying, along with primary dealers, the possibility of having extra auctions of variable rate bonds outside the regular auction schedule.
In what it described as a move to improve the security of the French market, the Treasury will reduce the payment delay for OAT and BTAN sales to one calendar week from July 1, 1997.
The payment delay is currently between three and four weeks for franc auctions at the moment.

From the first Treasury bill auction of 1997, which takes place on January 6, the payment date for T-bill auctions will be the Thursday following the sale. Treasury bill auctions usually take place on Mondays.
